sections.overview: The grey noddy is a small Pacific seabird in the tern family. Molecular phylogeny places it as the sister species of the blue noddy, listed separately here as Procelsterna cerulea.
sections.identification: It has a grey back and darker wings, with a much paler head and underside than the blue noddy.
sections.habitat: It forages in coastal waters and nests on remote Pacific islands, including rocky ledges and sheltered ground.
sections.diet: It takes small fish and marine invertebrates, including crustaceans and squid.
sections.behavior: It searches for prey by hovering or dipping close to the sea surface.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground or on rocky ledges and lays a single egg.
sections.ecology: Its island colonies and nearshore feeding connect nesting sites with the surrounding tropical marine environment.
sections.conservation: BirdLife assesses the grey noddy as Least Concern; its population total is uncertain because estimates are combined with those of the blue noddy.
